title: The 7 Best WiFi Calling Apps in 2026
summary: Using a WiFi connection for business calls is a smart move, but how do you pick the best WiFi calling app? Get details on the top options.
body_markdown:
The days of looking for a cell signal to make phone calls are over.[WiFi calling](https://www.quo.com/blog/what-is-wifi-calling/) — which allows you to easily reach your contacts using a WiFi connection — is becoming the norm for many businesses. Switching to WiFi calling is a simple way to save on phone plans and give your team the flexibility to call from any device, including[PCs](https://www.quo.com/blog/call-from-pc/) .


However, not all internet phones are equal. We’ll introduce you to seven of the best WiFi calling apps so you can choose a platform that fits all your business needs.


### WiFi calling apps roundup


**


- **Quo:** Best business phone solution
- **Google Voice:** Best for Google Workspace users
- **Google Meet:** Best for video calling
- **Burner:** Best for temporary phone numbers
- **WhatsApp:** Best for secure calls with other WhatsApp users
- **Viber:** Best for calls using a smartphone
- **Talkatone:** Best app for personal use

##


**7 best WiFi calling apps**


WiFi calling apps let you make calls over the internet with a quick download. They’re a good alternative to mobile telephone plans. Some allow unlimited calling and SMS, while others only let you call from app-to-app.


Certain WiFi calling apps on this list are best suited for personal use, like Burner, WhatsApp, and Viber, while others like Quo, Talkatone, and Google Voice can fit within a business context.


One big[advantage of WiFi calling](https://www.quo.com/blog/pros-and-cons-of-wifi-calling/) is that you don’t have to buy new Apple or Android devices or landlines for every team member or purchase expensive phone plans. The best WiFi calling apps also offer features that traditional phones can’t.


Here are seven of the best WiFi calling apps you can use to take your phone communications to the web with just a WiFi connection.

- Unlimited calling and texting to the US and Canada
- Sona AI receptionist
- Integrations with Zapier, Slack, and HubSpot
- Shared phone numbers
- Quick context in a single-view inbox
- Auto-attendant, or IVR, for inbound calls


#### Cons


- No verification through two-factor authentication*


**Nearly all virtual phone numbers share this problem. For safety reasons, companies like Facebook, Uber, and Google rarely let you authenticate accounts through a virtual phone number.*


Quo is a[VoIP phone service](https://www.quo.com/blog/best-voip-service/) that supports free calls and texts — both[SMS and MMS](https://www.quo.com/blog/sms-vs-mms/) — in the US and Canada from virtually any device. You can also make international calls for as little as two cents per minute. Check out our[international calling and texting rate page](https://www.quo.com/rates) for a full breakdown of the cost to call customers abroad.


What makes Quo stand out is its ability to function as more than a replacement for a physical phone. It makes business calls easier to manage. You can share phone numbers — including[toll-free](https://www.quo.com/toll-free-numbers) , Canadian, and US phone numbers — with your teammates so anyone who’s available can answer incoming calls and texts.


Every Quo plan lets you[schedule texts](https://www.quo.com/blog/how-to-schedule-texts/) so you can reach customers at a later time or date. You also have the option to set up auto-replies so customers get an immediate response even when you’re busy.


Quo also has Sona, your always-on AI receptionist. It can answer calls on your behalf using the knowledge you provide. Sona can also:


- Serve as a backup receptionist after hours or during weekends and holidays
- Capture leave information and record it
- Accurately answer business or product questions
- Transfer urgent calls that need to be escalated to someone on your team


You can integrate Quo with business apps like[Zapier](https://www.quo.com/blog/openphone-zapier-integration/) and[Slack](https://www.quo.com/blog/forward-texts-to-slack/) to streamline your workflows, along with other tools via the Quo API, or set up an[auto-attendant](https://www.quo.com/product/auto-attendant) to get clients to the right person faster.


Here’s what some of our customers say about Quo:

I haven’t run into any glitches or bugs so far, and customer support has been very quick and effective for setup and porting my old number.” —*[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/quo-quo/reviews/quo-review-13423051)

Any updates done to the website are immediately available on the app. The voicemail transcription can be sent to your email, and it is 100% correct (tested in English and Spanish)… Fully automated and intuitive. It took 45 minutes to get all the settings done and testing calls, voicemails, and text messages.” —*[G2](https://www.g2.com/products/quo-quo/reviews/quo-review-13120506)


Try Quo for a week to confirm it’s a great fit.[Sign up for a free seven-day trial](https://my.quo.com/signup) .

#### **Quo pricing**


- **Starter** : $15 per user per month for[unlimited calls](https://www.quo.com/features/unlimited-calls) in the US and Canada, on-demand call recording, shared phone numbers, one free local or toll-free US or Canadian number per user, and more

### ****2. Google Voice: Best for Google Workspace users****


#### Pros


- Free plan for personal use
- Integrates with other Google Workspace apps


#### Cons


- Limited business phone features


[Google Voice](https://www.quo.com/blog/google-voice-alternatives/) is a WiFi calling and texting app available on iPhones, Android phones, and the web. The free and paid personal plans are only available in the US and aren’t designed for business, since each account can only have one user and phone number. It also lacks business features like ring groups.


There are significant differences between Google Voice Personal and Google Voice for Business. Google Voice’s personal plans offer free calling and texting within the US, but only allow you to record inbound calls on demand. It also doesn’t allow three-way conferencing or auto-attendants.[Google Voice for Business](https://www.quo.com/blog/google-voice-for-business/) is available in 14 countries, offers ring groups, and integrates with Gmail, Google Meet, and Google Calendar.


But if you’re not part of Google Workspace, you need to purchase a Workspace and a Voice subscription to access the app. That’s a total of at least $17 — $10 for the lowest plan of Google Voice for Business and $7 for a Google Workspace subscription.


While both Google Voice for personal and business offer voicemail transcriptions and integrations with Google Calendar, Google Sheets, Google Docs, and Google Meet — which puts it a step ahead of your average cell phone — you won’t get much more support for your company’s needs, even with their[business phone app](https://www.quo.com/blog/best-business-phone-number-apps/) . You can get more bang for your buck and bring more of your tech stack together to save time with other apps.


Some users value Google Voice for its convenience like this reviewer on[Capterra](https://www.capterra.com/p/210592/Voice/#99a1c38d-feb0-480c-ab37-3626b02659b4/) :


*“Google Voice gives me a separate phone number that I can use for calls and text messages without needing another phone. I like being able to access it from both my phone and computer, and having calls, messages, and voicemail connected to the same account is convenient.”*


However, this same user admits that Google Voice can be too simple:


*“The calling and messaging experience is more basic than a regular mobile service, and occasionally notifications or incoming calls do not feel quite as seamless as using the phone’s native number.”*


#### Key features of Google Voice


**


- Free unlimited calls to the US and from the US to Canada
- Free unlimited texts in the US
- Integrations with Google Calendar and Google Meet require an upgrade
- Auto-attendant requires an upgrade
- Call recording requires an upgrade


#### Google Voice pricing


**


Google Voice has six plans in total: three Personal plans and three Google Voice for Business plans.


These three Personal plans don’t require a Google Workspace subscription.


- **Personal:** One free user with one number for unlimited calling and messaging to the US and Canada
- **Starter with Voice:** $10 for one user per month for on-demand call recording and desk phone support
- **Voice Standard:** $20 for one user per month for AI note-taking and auto-attendants


These Google Voice for Business plans let you add more users to your account if you have a team. All require a $7-per-user-per-month Google Workspace subscription:


- **Voice Starter:** $10 per user per month with a maximum of 10 seats
- **Voice Standard:** $20 per user per month for unlimited seats, multi-level auto-attendant,[ring groups](https://www.quo.com/features/ring-groups) , call delegation, and custom hold audio
- **Voice Premier: $** 30 per user per month for unlimited seats, advanced reporting,[automatic call recording](https://www.quo.com/product/call-recording/automatic-call-recording) , and the ability to get additional numbers outside your home country


### ****3. Google Meet: Best for video calling****


#### Pros


- Record meetings
- Have one-to-one calls for up to 24 hours


#### Cons


- No desktop app


Google Meet is a free WiFi calling app that supports video and voice calls. Using Meet’s Android, iOS, or web app, you can make one-on-one calls that can last for up to 24 hours and group calls for up to 60 minutes with up to three participants.


While Google Meet is one of the best WiFi calling apps for consumers, it isn’t built for business use. There’s no way to call non-Meet users, which means you can’t reliably reach all your clients. Also, Meet doesn’t offer free phone numbers. You’ll need to use your[personal phone number](https://www.quo.com/blog/using-your-personal-phone-number-for-business-heres-why-you-shouldnt/) or email address to sign up, and users will contact you using your existing contact details.


To access Google Meet’s premium features, you need a Google Workspace subscription, which starts at $7 per user per month. If you already pay for a Google One Premium plan, you can use Google Meet features like noise cancellation and call recording, which are still limited.


Unless you need to video call your clients as a fish or a cactus, the app’s only special feature — its augmented reality, or AR, effects — won’t really help your team succeed.


#### Key features of Google Meet


**


- Free unlimited video and voice calls with Meet users
- Digital whiteboarding
- Breakout rooms


#### Google Meet pricing


**


Google Meet’s free plan includes unlimited calls and meetings with other Google Meet users, plus live captions, screen sharing, and web or mobile access.


Google Meet is also bundled into the Google Workspace for Business plan. You need this to call US numbers using Google Meet. Here are the current Google Workspace for Business plans:


- **Business Starter:** $7 per user per month for up to 100 participants for business email, security and management controls, US or international dial-in phone numbers, and digital whiteboarding
- **Business Standard:** $14 per user per month for up to 150 participants for noise cancellation, meeting recordings saved to Google Drive, and polling and Q&A
- **Business Plus:** $22 per user per month for up to 500 participants for attendance tracking and breakout rooms
- **Enterprise:** Contact for pricing for up to 1,000 participants for in-domain live streaming and hand raising


### **4. Burner: Best app for temporary phone numbers**


#### Pros


- Buy up to 100 numbers at once on iOS
- Unlimited calls and texts


#### Cons


- Not ideal for business use
- No integrations
- No call recordings
- No auto-attendants


Burner is a WiFi calling app that’s focused on protecting user privacy. It’s available for iOS and Android. Users can get unlimited calling and texting within the US and Canada and can use spam-blocking to prevent unwanted calls.


Burner apps let you switch between numbers and delete alternate phone numbers at any time. These are ideal for temporary situations like traveling or if you want to keep your real number safe from robocalls and spam.


You can download the Burner app from the App Store, the Google Play Store, or directly from their website. Each differs in their price and how many numbers it supports:


- The web app supports one to three phone numbers
- The Android app supports one, three, and 10 phone numbers
- The iOS app supports up to 100 phone numbers


We *don’t* recommend Burner for business purposes. Temporary numbers aren’t good for businesses that want to establish long-term relationships with customers. Burner doesn’t come with any essential business features like call recording, integrations, or call transfers. You don’t get shared phone numbers, either, so teammates can’t help you manage calls.


#### Key features of Burner


**


- Unlimited calls and texts in the US and Canada
- Multiple temporary phone numbers per person
- Text message auto-replies
- Anonymous texting and calling


#### Burner pricing


**


Burner’s prices change depending on where you buy them:


- **Web Standard:** $3.99 per user per month for a private number, anonymous texting and calling, and number switching
- **Web Premium:** $5.83 per user per month for VPN, video messages, and phone ID lookup
- **App Store Standard:** $5.00 per user per month billed annually for one private phone number and anonymous texting and calling
- **App Store Premium:** $7.50 per user per month billed annually for one line with VPN, video messages, and voicemail transcription
- **Android Store Standard:** $5.00 per user per month billed annually for unlimited calls, texts, and MMS, and includes a private phone number
- **Android Store Premium:** $7.50 per user per month billed annually for one line with VPN, video messages, and voicemail transcription


### ****5. WhatsApp: Best for secure calling with other WhatsApp users****


#### Pros


- Voice and video calls with up to 32 people
- Free text messaging


#### Cons


- No pricing plans or upgrades for business features


WhatsApp Messenger is an instant messaging app that’s used by over two billion people around the world to send free text messages — including multimedia like pictures, GIFs, and documents — and to call without international rates.


It supports free video and voice calls through its mobile or desktop app using your WiFi or data connection. It also provides end-to-end encryption, ensuring only you and the person you’re calling or texting with can read your communication history. The caveat is that you need an existing phone number to use WhatsApp, so you can’t create a[separate phone number](https://www.quo.com/blog/get-second-phone-number/) for your business calls and texts.


WhatsApp Business lets you build out a company profile and catalog for WhatsApp users to see. You can set up automated replies for incoming texts, but you won’t get any features for[call management](https://www.quo.com/product/call-management) .


#### Key features of WhatsApp


**


- Free unlimited video calls, voice calls, and texts (data charges may apply)
- Group calls with up to 32 participants
- [Automated texts](https://www.quo.com/product/messaging/automated-text-messages) (WhatsApp Business only)
- Text message templates (WhatsApp Business only)


#### WhatsApp pricing


**


Free to use


### ****6. Viber: Best for calls using a smartphone****


#### Pros


- Share stickers and GIFs
- Set disappearing messages


#### Cons


- Have to pay to call anyone outside the Viber network


Viber is often listed as one of the best free calling apps since it offers video calls, voice calls, and messages. Much like WhatsApp and Google Meet, it’s designed for Viber users to communicate through one-on-one and group chats. While you may see Viber marketed as free, you’ll have to pay per minute or pay for a subscription if you want to call anyone who doesn’t use Viber.


Viber is a pretty bare-bones app, even if you pay. It’s designed for personal use, so while you’ll get fun features like self-destructing messages, the ability to share stickers and polls you can text, you won’t get any features modern businesses need.


#### Key features of Viber


**


- Free unlimited video calls, voice calls, and texts with Viber users
- Disappearing messages
- Group chats
- Delete and edit seen messages


#### Viber pricing


**


**Viber for personal use:**


- Free to use
- Rates vary by country to call non-Viber users


**Viber for business:**


- Contact vendor for pricing for real-time customer support, an in-app call option for customers that allows them to contact your business for free, and more


### ****7. Talkatone: Best for personal use****


#### Pros


- Free US phone number
- Free calls and texts to and from US and Canadian numbers


#### Cons


- Can’t change caller ID after you’ve created an account


Talkatone is a WiFi calling app that lets you make calls on Android tablets, iPads, smartphones, and iPods. It offers unlimited access to calls, group chats, and texts wherever you are, which is useful for reps who travel a lot and need access to their conversation history on the go. You can also choose a free USphone number when you sign up with Talkatone, a feature that’s ideal for companies that have customers in the US..


However, Talkatone lacks features your business might need to scale. For example, you can’t send text messages to international numbers, and you can’t port your number over to Talkatone. The app also contains ads that are only removed when you upgrade to its premium subscription, which costs $3.99 per user per month.


#### Key features of Talkatone


**


- Free calling and texting to any US or Canadian phone number
- Free international calls between Talkatone users
- Free US number included
- Call forwarding requires an upgrade


#### Talkatone pricing


**


- **Free plan** : Calling most US and Canadian numbers is completely free
- **Talkatone Plus** : $3.99 per user per month for no daily messaging limits (other limits may apply), forwarding your calls to any US or Canadian number, listening to your voicemails in high-quality audio, and more


##


**Why use a WiFi calling app?**


There are a number of reasons to use a[WiFi calling app](https://www.quo.com/blog/pros-and-cons-of-wifi-calling/) over a traditional phone line. Here’s when it might be more practical:


### **More than just a phone call**


Certain WiFi calling apps can do more than just call or text. They also offer other business-friendly features like assigning employees to a shared phone number, routing calls, or setting up AI-powered virtual receptionists.


### **Save on calling and messaging**


One of the WiFi calling apps’ biggest advantages is saving money on calls and texts — especially for second lines, international calls, or business use. Most apps on this list offer unlimited calling and texting to US phone numbers or other app users.


### **More connection options**


Cellular strength can be spotty and inconsistent. You might be indoors, or your provider may not have good coverage in that area. But the WiFi app will work fine as long as there’s an available internet connection.


### **No additional hardware required**


WiFi calling apps are easy to set up. Just install the app on your device — no need for specialized equipment or technicians. You can call from a PC or Mac, or from an Android or iOS phone.

**FAQs**


****​​Is WiFi calling really free?****


WiFi calling is really free when you use an app like Facebook Messenger or WhatsApp. Remember, the person you’re trying to call must also have a Facebook Messenger or WhatsApp account.


Quo is the best[WiFi texting](https://www.quo.com/blog/best-wifi-texting-apps/) and calling app. From $15 per user per month, you can call and text customers in the US and Canada as much as you want — and they don’t need an account.


****Do you need an app for WiFi calling?****


No, you don’t need an app for WiFi calling. This is because your smartphone can have built-in WiFi calling, which lets you make and receive voice calls over a WiFi network or hotspot instead of using your cellular network.


Here are the steps you need to follow to enable WiFi calling on a smartphone like an iPhone:
1. Open the settings menu. Navigate to **Phone** > **WiFi Calling** .
2. Slide the button next to Wi-Fi Calling on **This iPhone** .
3. The slider turns green when WiFi calling is enabled.


****What is the best app for calling abroad?****


The best app for calling abroad will have the features your business needs. With Quo, for example, you can make international calls that cost you a fraction of what you could pay with a traditional carrier.


****How do you set up WiFi calling on a smartphone?****


Here are the steps to set up WiFi calling on a smartphone using Quo:


1.[Sign up](https://my.quo.com/signup) to create your account.
2. Verify your identity and provide credit card information.
3. Download the Quo mobile app on your Android or iPhone.
4. Start making calls from your smartphone.
